commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Add an option to limit the bytes a dispatch binds (#25299)

Some targets need to have every buffer a dispatch binds mapped to a
limited address space, e.g. 32 bit. There may also be other limits on
the amount of mapped memory at the same time. Fusion can form dispatches
that cannot run, even when each binding fits into the max allocation
size. For instance, once a large constant is split into shards (see
`iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`), elementwise fusion merges the
per-shard embedding lookups back into one op that reads every shard.

This adds `--iree-dispatch-creation-max-dispatch-binding-size` (default
0, no limit) and a `max-dispatch-binding-size` option on the passes that
grow dispatches:

* ElementwiseOpFusion, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FuseMultiUseElementwiseProducer, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FormDispatchRegions, in `FusionGroup::wouldExceedOperandLimit`, next
to the existing limit on the number of operands, so that all producer
and consumer fusion decisions are covered,
* CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions, through
`CloneableIntoDispatchOptions` in `getCloneableOps`,
* FuseHorizontalContractions, which adds a weight and a result to the
  fused contraction for each contraction it merges,
* ConvertTensorToFlow, for producers cloned into the dispatches it
  creates for slices.

The bytes are estimated by `IREE::Flow::getDispatchBindingBytes`: the
statically shaped tensors that the ops read from outside (as operands or
captured in their regions), plus their results that are used outside.
Loads of the same global count once; `tensor.empty`, `linalg.fill` and
splat constants are not bindings. Producers cloned into a dispatch
contribute only what they read, because those remain in place for their
other users. Fusion decisions count the producers that
CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions will clone into the dispatch later
(e.g. dequantization ops) by what they read, not by their results. A
fusion or clone is refused only if the dispatch would then bind more
than the limit and more than it did without it, so fusions that shrink a
dispatch already over the limit still happen.

Dynamically shaped tensors count as zero bytes, so the limit only covers
static shapes, which includes all constants.

static shapes, which includes all constants.

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to ba6c16a6 (#25309)

Updates torch-mlir from its November 4 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@ba6c16a6`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/ba6c16a6fbcd92c0a46759aacf31a324ccdf28a1),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@ba6c16a6`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/ba6c16a6fbcd92c0a46759aacf31a324ccdf28a1)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261120`).

The integration branch is plain upstream torch-mlir with no extra
commits. The previous one only bumped torch-mlir's own LLVM and
StableHLO submodules, which IREE does not use. This revision builds
against IREE's current LLVM without changes.

ONNX op test expectations:

- `test_div_uint8` is now an expected compile failure on Vulkan.
llvm/torch-mlir#4896 fixed uint8 division to use `arith.divui`, and the
SPIR-V conversion does not support `arith.divui` on emulated i8
(#25316). The test passed before only because its inputs are below 128,
where signed and unsigned division agree.

The `sharktank_tests :: cpu_task` failure is unrelated. The job fails to
download the test artifacts from Azure (`AuthorizationFailure`), and
main (14e6942619) fails the same way.

Make attention end-to-end tests reviewable by hand

not be checked by a reader, and whose long lines broke review tooling. They

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Add an option to limit the bytes a dispatch binds (#25299)

Some targets need to have every buffer a dispatch binds mapped to a
limited address space, e.g. 32 bit. There may also be other limits on
the amount of mapped memory at the same time. Fusion can form dispatches
that cannot run, even when each binding fits into the max allocation
size. For instance, once a large constant is split into shards (see
`iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`), elementwise fusion merges the
per-shard embedding lookups back into one op that reads every shard.

This adds `--iree-dispatch-creation-max-dispatch-binding-size` (default
0, no limit) and a `max-dispatch-binding-size` option on the passes that
grow dispatches:

* ElementwiseOpFusion, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FuseMultiUseElementwiseProducer, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FormDispatchRegions, in `FusionGroup::wouldExceedOperandLimit`, next
to the existing limit on the number of operands, so that all producer
and consumer fusion decisions are covered,
* CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions, through
`CloneableIntoDispatchOptions` in `getCloneableOps`,
* FuseHorizontalContractions, which adds a weight and a result to the
  fused contraction for each contraction it merges,
* ConvertTensorToFlow, for producers cloned into the dispatches it
  creates for slices.

The bytes are estimated by `IREE::Flow::getDispatchBindingBytes`: the
statically shaped tensors that the ops read from outside (as operands or
captured in their regions), plus their results that are used outside.
Loads of the same global count once; `tensor.empty`, `linalg.fill` and
splat constants are not bindings. Producers cloned into a dispatch
contribute only what they read, because those remain in place for their
other users. Fusion decisions count the producers that
CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions will clone into the dispatch later
(e.g. dequantization ops) by what they read, not by their results. A
fusion or clone is refused only if the dispatch would then bind more
than the limit and more than it did without it, so fusions that shrink a
dispatch already over the limit still happen.

Dynamically shaped tensors count as zero bytes, so the limit only covers
static shapes, which includes all constants.
